# IBM i MCP Server v0.7.0-alpha.0

This is a pre-release of 0.7.0, published under the npm dist-tag `next`. `latest` stays at 0.6.2. It contains breaking changes to HTTP authentication and session configuration (see below). It is also the first release published by the new release workflow.

```bash
npx -y @ibm/ibmi-mcp-server@0.7.0-alpha.0 --transport http --tools ./tools
npm install -g @ibm/ibmi-cli@0.7.0-alpha.0
```

## Overview

- **MCP SDK v2** — The server moves to `@modelcontextprotocol/server` v2 and serves current and 2025-era clients from one stateless endpoint
- **Sign on with your IBM i profile** — `MCP_AUTH_MODE=oauth` makes the server its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server, and every tool runs its SQL as the signed-on user
- **SSH connections** — A source with an SSH key reaches Db2 for i over SSH, with no Mapepire daemon on port 8076
- **CLI sessions over SSH** — The `ibmi` CLI keeps an SSH session open between commands on SSH systems

[Configuration](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/configuration) | [IBM i sign-on](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/server-config/oauth-ibmi-signon) | [CLI configuration](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/cli/configuration)

---

## New Features

### Built-in IBM i sign-on

With `MCP_AUTH_MODE=oauth` and no `OAUTH_ISSUER_URL`, the server is its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server. Users sign on at its page with an IBM i profile and password, and every tool runs its SQL on a connection signed on as that user. Passwords are held only as AES-256-GCM ciphertext in memory, tokens are stored as hashes, and nothing is written to disk. Privileged profiles are refused by default.

With `OAUTH_ISSUER_URL` set, the server is instead an OAuth resource server for an external identity provider.

Documentation: [IBM i sign-on](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/server-config/oauth-ibmi-signon)

Reference: [#257](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/257)

### SSH connections to IBM i

A connection uses SSH when it has an SSH key. The server opens an SSH session and starts `mapepire-server` on demand, so no Mapepire daemon needs to run. SSH uses key authentication only; a password is never sent over SSH. Set `DB2i_SSH_KEY` for the built-in tools and every YAML source, or `ssh-key` on a single source:

```yaml
sources:
  dev:
    host: dev.example.com
    user: MYUSER
    ssh-key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    ssh-host-key-sha256: SHA256:AbC...

  prod:
    host: prod.example.com
    user: ${PROD_USER}
    password: ${PROD_PASS}
```

Pin the host key with `ssh-host-key-sha256` on a source or `DB2i_SSH_HOST_KEY_SHA256` in the environment. `DB2i_SSH_PORT`, `DB2i_SSH_PASSPHRASE` and `DB2i_SSH_TECHNIQUE` apply to every SSH connection.

Documentation: [Configuration](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/configuration)

Reference: [#255](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/255), [#265](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/265)

### CLI: SSH systems with a session that stays open

A CLI system with an SSH key uses SSH, and the first command opens a session that later commands reuse instead of reconnecting. The session closes after 10 minutes without a command.

```bash
ibmi system add dev --host dev.example.com --user MYUSER \
  --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 --ssh-host-key-sha256 SHA256:AbC...
ibmi sql "values current server"    # opens the session
ibmi sql "values current server"    # reuses it
ibmi system status                  # transport and session of each system
ibmi system disconnect dev          # close it (--all for every system)
ibmi sql "values 1" --fresh         # connect for this command only
```

All commands on one system share one SQL job while the session is open, so `SET SCHEMA` and temporary tables carry over between commands.

Documentation: [CLI configuration](https://ibm-d95bab6e.mintlify.app/cli/configuration)

Reference: [#268](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/268)

## Breaking Changes

- **The server is always stateless.** `MCP_SESSION_MODE` and `MCP_STATEFUL_SESSION_STALE_TIMEOUT_MS` are removed. There is no `Mcp-Session-Id`, and `GET` and `DELETE` on the MCP endpoint return 405.
- **JWT auth mode is removed.** `MCP_AUTH_MODE=jwt`, `MCP_AUTH_SECRET_KEY`, `DEV_MCP_CLIENT_ID` and `DEV_MCP_SCOPES` are gone. Use `MCP_AUTH_MODE=oauth`.
- **Startup fails fast.** An invalid environment variable, an unknown log level, a busy port, or a YAML file that fails to parse or validate now stops startup instead of logging a warning.
- **`MCP_AUTH_MODE=ibmi` is deprecated.** It behaves as before, with a startup warning and a `Deprecation` response header. Move to `MCP_AUTH_MODE=oauth`.

Reference: [#257](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/257)

## Bug Fixes

- `DB2i_JDBC_OPTIONS` now applies to per-user authenticated pools ([#247](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/247))
- Reloading YAML tools no longer leaks connection pools ([#246](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/246))
- Parameter markers inside string literals and SQL comments are no longer treated as parameters ([#243](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/243))
- `/healthz` requests are no longer written to the access log ([#197](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/197))
- `enabled: false` YAML tools are not registered, and built-in tools are no longer capped at 100 rows ([#257](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/257))
- Dependency security alerts remediated ([#226](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/226), [#235](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/235), [#236](https://github.com/IBM/ibmi-mcp-server/pull/236))
